request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A held person's claims, and held claims, now count in every total again: claimed, due-totals,
overdue, the period figures, backing, the rollup lines. The only thing a hold still does is in the
pools: a held person gets no cut and their share is spread over the others, as before.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now only affect the pools: a held person, or a held claim, counts in every total again. A held person still gets no cut, and their share is spread over the others. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

The change is in two places, one on the server and one on the screen:
- **Server** (`Person.java`): `leftOutLive` no longer leaves out a claim because the claim is held or falls in one of the person's holds. Being deferred, or belonging to a retired person, still leaves an open claim out. This feeds the rollup lines (person and sheet totals), the period figures and statements.
- **Screen** (`features/claims/api.ts`): `liveClaims` has the same hold check removed, so every total on the page counts held claims (due, overdue, backing, period, month, tag and crew totals). `claimedClaims` now just reuses `liveClaims`, since the two no longer differ.

The pool code (`PoolRepository`) still reads person holds to decide who gets no cut, and I didn't touch it. No stored data or schema change was needed; the claim's `held` flag and the person's holds are still saved and shown as before. I also updated the comments that described the old rule.

probe.probe_text:
Nothing was changed. The money logic (`Dues`, the rates and settings helpers, the totals), the front-end figure code and `Person`/`Claim` I read myself. The per-action rules (permissions, period checks, imports, merges, pools) were summarised by three read-only sub-agents. I spot-checked parts of that, not every line. # 1. Figures and the rules behind them ## Per claim (`claim-row-`) | Shown | How it is decided | |---|---| | `claim-number` | Given only when a claim opens. A DRAFT or REVIEW claim has none, and a VOID claim keeps its number. `ClaimNumbers.next` picks the scheme. If `period-numbering-from` is set and the sheet's today is on or after it, the number is `-` for the period its **due-by** falls in, or `X-` if it is in no period. Otherwise it is `FY-`, shared by every sheet in the tree and restarting each fiscal year (`fiscal-start-month`, default 1). Reassigning a claim, transferring a person or cloning a sheet gives it a new number. | | `claim-amount` | Two decimals, and may be negative. A negative amount is a **correction**. It must name in `corrects` a SETTLED claim of the same person, and may not exceed what is left of that claim (`Corrections`). A claim with lines has the lines' total as its amount (sum of qty × unit). | | `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is added. It is the *terms*-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`BusinessDays.dueBy`). Terms come from the person's own terms, else `terms-`, else `terms` (default 14), as they stand on the sheet's today (`termsToday`). Adding a holiday later works the due-by out again (`refixDueBys`) for claims that are not SETTLED, VOID or DELETED. Re-dating a claim or changing terms later does not move it. | | `claim-due` | `Dues.shown` on the server and `claimDue` in the front end; see "How due is worked out" below. It shows `n/a` when there is no rate. | | `claim-overdue` | OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `lateFrom` (due-by + `grace-` days) is before the sheet's today. | | `claim-status` | DRAFT → OPEN, or → REVIEW above `review-threshold`. OPEN → SETTLED, or → PENDING when a clerk settles above the clerk limit. PENDING → SETTLED (approve) or → OPEN (reject). DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW → VOID. DRAFT → DELETED → DRAFT, the restore allowed only on the same sheet today it was deleted (`ClaimStatus.moveTo`). | | `claim-deferred` / `-until` | A claim is deferred while it is OPEN (or VOID, if voided while deferred) and `deferredUntil` is after the sheet's today. | | `claim-stated` | Bound by the person's last statement. A bound claim shows and totals `statedDue`. | | `claim-waived`, `claim-held`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-proofs[-receipt/photo]`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-batch`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-period`, `claim-review-late` | `claim-late-entry`: added while its due-by's period was soft-closed. `claim-period`: the period its **due-by** falls in. `claim-review-late`: the REVIEW day + `review-sla` is before today. `claim-batch`: the bulk-settle batch number. | ### How due is worked out (`Dues.of` / `charge` / `shown`, mirrored in `rates/api.ts`) 1. A frozen `settledDue` wins. Otherwise a statement's `statedDue` wins. Otherwise the due is **live**. 2. **Live figure** = amount × rate% ÷ 100, rounded to 2 decimals. - The rate is `RateRepository.inForce` / `rateOn` for the person's grade **on the claim's date**. - It is the rate with the latest from-date on or before that date. If that rate has ended, or there is none, the parent sheet's rates are used, up to 3 levels, then the clone source's. - A forward-only rate applies only to claims with an id above `claimsAfter`. 3. **Rounding** (`Late.rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`) uses the claim's `roundDate`: its own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. The `rounding` setting in force on that date decides; with none set, dates before `policy-date` round HALF_UP and dates on or after it HALF_EVEN. A blank `policy-date` means the sheet's today. 4. **Floor**: the figure is raised to at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). Corrections have no floor. 5. **Late charge**: - One charge for each full 30 days since `lateFrom`. - Each charge is the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary, applied to the floored figure plus the earlier charges (it compounds), rounded each time. - There is no charge on a correction, on a claim that is not OPEN or PENDING, on a deferred claim, or after a waiver. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle or approve** freezes `settledDue`, late charge included. Settle can be dated `on=` a past date and then uses the figure as it stood then (`AsOfStore`). - **Resettle** (steward only) freezes it again at today's live figure. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every counting claim of the person to its due as shown at that moment. It unbinds the rest. A statement can be taken as of a past date. - Cancelling a statement (steward only) unbinds the claims. The figures of the earlier statement are not restored. - Split, reassign and transfer drop the binding. Reject and merge keep it. - **Closing or soft-closing a period** fixes each person's `personTotals` and `personCarried` for it, and the period's total (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`). Reopening unfixes them. - **Period membership** is by due-by, not by the claim's date. ## Per person (`person-row-`), all computed in `People.tsx` from `claims/api.ts`, `rates/api.ts` and `periods/api.ts` **Which claims count** - `counts` / `isCounting`: OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. - `liveClaims` / `countsLive` then leave out: - deferred claims; - open claims not bound by a statement, once the sheet's today has reached the person's retirement date (`isRetiredReached`). - A **hold** leaves nothing out of the totals; it matters only in pools. Several comments say the opposite (see section 2). | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `person-claimed` | Sum of the **amounts** of live counting claims, leaving out claims that name another (`correctsAnother`). | | `person-due-total` | `personDue`: the sum of the claims' dues, n/a ones skipped, capped at `cap` (the value in force on the sheet's today). It shows `n/a` when the person's grade has no rate today and no claim keeps a figure (frozen, bound, or live at an old grade or date). | | `person-excess` | The amount above `cap`. | | `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total` | `splitDues`: dues of SETTLED claims, and dues of OPEN/PENDING claims. | | `person-aged-0-30` / `31-60` / `61` | `agedDues`: open claims bucketed by days since their date. | | `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | `overdue`: count and due total of overdue claims. | | `person-period-

-due-total` | Once the period is fixed, the frozen figure. Otherwise the live dues of claims whose due-by is in the period and whose status at the end of the period's last day (read from the claim log, `statusOn`) was counting. | | `person-period-

-carried` | Once fixed, the frozen figure. Otherwise the opening balance (`importOpenings`) plus claims due in earlier periods that were still open at this period's end. | | `person-active` | Has a live open claim dated within the last 30 days. | | `person-cut-total` | Sum of the person's pool cuts (rules below). | | `person-backing` | Patrons split 100.00 equally (HALF_EVEN, the remainder to the first named). Each patron's SETTLED frozen dues dated within the last 90 days, times that patron's share. | | `person-grade` / `person-terms` | The grade, and the person's own terms, in force on the sheet's today (`gradeOn` / `termsOn`). | | `person-retired` / `-from` / retirement lines | Claims dated after the retirement date, or inside a past retirement, are refused (`retiredBefore`). | | Statement figures | `person-statement-count`, `person-stated-total`, `person-statement-date`, statement lines. The total is `n/a` when there was no rate. | | Snapshot lines | One per change of the sheet's today: the due-total on the day being left. | | `person-hold`, `person-flag-shown` (until ≥ today), `person-approver`, `person-clashing` (name or alias used on another sheet of the tree), `person-watched` | Flags. | ## Sheet totals (front end) - **Due total** (`rollup-due-total`, `header-due-total`) and **overdue total**: `trimmedSum` of the per-person figures. With 3 or more figures, the single highest and single lowest are dropped. - **Untrimmed totals**: the `classic-due-total`, the settled, open and aged rollups, and the month, tag, grade and period totals are plain sums. - **Claimed total**: plain sum of claimed amounts. - **Consolidated**: sums the figures across the sheet's descendant sheets. - The server keeps its own copy of these totals in `Rollup.java`, which writes the `ROLLUP`, `TOTALS` and `ALERT` (`alert-threshold`) audit lines. ## Pools - Members on a hold that covers today, retired members and members whose dates exclude today get no cut. - Cuts happen only when there is a `pot` and the members' shares total exactly 100.00. - Each cut is pot × share ÷ (sum of cutting shares), rounded HALF_EVEN. The remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut, the latest added on a tie. - A crew pool gives equal shares, the remainder to the lead. ## Who may do what - **Roles**: `clerk` (the default for any name), `steward`, `viewer`. A delegation makes a user a steward while it covers the sheet's today. - **`RefuseViewer`**: an archived sheet or a viewer is refused every change. - **`Permissions`** (`perm-`; a blank entry means the standing rule): open, settle, void and close are clerk + steward; reassign and reopen are steward only. - **Four-eyes**: the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, may not settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit** (`clerk-limit[-]`): a clerk settling above it sends the claim to PENDING. - **Approve and reject**: a steward, or the person's `approver`. - **Proof threshold** (`proof-threshold[-]`, `proof-kinds`): a claim above it needs proofs before settle or approve. - **`note-threshold`**: a claim above it needs a note to open. - **Period `cap`**: the most OPEN/PENDING claims a person may have per period. - **Flagged person**: only a steward may open their claims. - **Steward only**: waive, re-date, resettle, void a SETTLED claim (within `SETTLED_DAYS = 7`), merge, transfer, undo a transfer (same day only), flag, cancel a statement, lock or unlock a period, archive, clone. - **Not checked at all**: settings and roles have no role check beyond the viewer guard, so a clerk can make themselves a steward. ## Periods - **Closed**: any change to a claim whose due-by is inside it is refused with 423 (`requireOpen`). - **Soft-closed**: figures are fixed, but claims can still be changed; a new claim is marked `lateEntry`. - **Locked**: only blocks reopening. - **`grace-days`**: auto-closes a period once its end + N days is before a new sheet today. - **Sheet today**: changing it writes snapshots, releases claim editor locks, auto-closes periods and moves every date rule. A `shown-asof` view replays the sheet as it stood and is read-only. ## Imports, holds and the rest - **Import people**: matched by name or alias. New people are added; existing people get their terms and contact updated, and a changed grade applies from today. The default grade is `default-grade`. One bad line refuses the whole import. - **Paste claims**: a line matching an existing DRAFT updates it; otherwise a claim is added and **opened**. It is all or nothing. - **Import rates / openings**: all or nothing. An opening is added to the person's carried figure; on a closed period it shows only after a reopen and re-close. - **Person hold**: affects only pool cuts. - **Claim hold**: display only. - **Merge**: claims, pool shares, period totals, statements, patrons and crews move to the surviving person. - **Transfer**: claims are renumbered on the new sheet, and statements are set aside (restored on undo). # 2. How hard it was to follow It was hard. Nothing about the figures lives in one place a new developer could pick up: - **The due rules are written twice.** The server has them in Java (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `PeriodClosing`, `SettleClaim` and five more call sites). The screen works out every figure it shows again in TypeScript (`rates/api.ts`, `claims/api.ts`, `periods/api.ts`, and about ten components each repeating the same setup). - **The other rules are spread across about 300 one-method classes** wired by YAML, so knowing which checks run, and in what order, means reading the pipeline files. - **The code comments contradict each other and the code**, so they can't be trusted: - **Holds.** The code says a hold leaves nothing out of the totals; the comments in `People.tsx`, `TakeStatement` and `hold.POST.yml` say it does. - **Which terms set the due-by.** `Claim.java` says those in force on the claim's date; the code uses those in force on the sheet's today. - **Which period a claim is in.** Some comments say by its date; the code uses its due-by. - **What "overdue" covers.** Some comments say OPEN claims only; the code includes PENDING. - **Similar names mean different things.** `grace-days` auto-closes periods, while `grace-` shifts lateness. A period's "cap" limits a person's open claims in it, while the sheet's `cap` caps a person's due-total.
